home.heroTaglineTranslation: May my mind be filled with auspicious resolve
home.heroSubtitle: Uplifting Vedic Gurukulas through Seva, Śraddhā & Saṁskāra
home.heroDescription: With the boundless grace of the Jagadgurus of Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri, we are devoted to supporting Veda Gurukulas and sustaining the timeless Guru–Shishya Parampara.
home.vedaVidyaSubtitle: The Vedas are the foundation of Sanātana Dharma — an unbroken oral tradition spanning millennia, preserved through the sacred bond of Guru and Shishya.
home.vedaVidyaShlokaTranslation: Rooted in the four Vedas, Dharma stands eternal — nourishing life, order, and truth.
home.vedaVrukshaAlt: Veda Vriksha — The Tree of Vedic Knowledge showing the four Vedas (Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, Atharvaveda), their shakhas, and the six Vedangas
home.whyGurukulasSubtitle: Adi Shankaracharya's timeless injunction: 'Let the Veda be studied daily.'
home.whyGurukulasPara1: Inspired by the timeless injunction of Adi Shankaracharya — {shloka} ('let the Veda be studied daily') — Veda Gurukulas stand as sacred institutions that preserve the very heartbeat of Sanātana Dharma. Rooted in the venerable Guru–Śiṣya Paramparā, they are not merely centres of learning, but sanctuaries where knowledge is lived, discipline is cultivated, and saṁskāra is imbibed through constant guidance and practice.
home.whyGurukulasPara2: In an age of rapid change, they remain timeless beacons, ensuring that the wisdom of the Ṛṣis continues to illuminate generations with purity, authenticity, and unwavering continuity.
home.whyGurukulasPara3: In humble alignment with this sacred ideal, Śrī Śivasaṅkalpa Vṛnda is devoted to supporting and strengthening Veda Gurukulas. Through dedicated efforts toward the welfare of Vedic students and Adhyāpakas, the Vṛnda seeks to contribute — however modestly — to the continuity of this timeless heritage, for the benefit of society and for {lokaKalyana}.
home.gurukulasTitle: Gurukulas We Are Privileged to Serve
home.gurukulasSubtitle: We work directly with Vedic Gurukulas in Karnataka, understanding their needs and providing sustained support.
home.maharudraShlokaTranslation: That which melts away suffering — that is Rudra.
home.sringeriImageAlt: Sri Sharada Devi, Adi Shankaracharya, Jagadguru Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahasannidhanam, and Jagadguru Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam of Sringeri Sharada Peetham
home.sringeriPara: The name 'Sri Shivasankalpa' was bestowed as a blessing by His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam of the Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri. Sri Shivasankalpa Vṛnda operates with the boundless grace and divine blessings of His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahasannidhanam and His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam.
home.sringeriNote: The Vṛnda considers the blessings and approval of the Sringeri Jagadgurus as paramount in all its endeavours.

about.heroSubtitle: Uplifting Vedic Gurukulas through Seva, Śraddhā & Saṁskāra
about.storyPara1: Across India, Vedic Gurukulas quietly sustain one of humanity's oldest living traditions. Within their modest walls, young students rise before dawn to learn the Vedas through an unbroken oral lineage — guided by Adhyāpakas who have given their lives to mastering it.
about.storyPara2: Yet most of these Gurukulas operate with limited funding, aging infrastructure, and little public visibility — and the very teachers who sustain the tradition are often the least recognised.
about.storyPara3: Sri Shivasankalpa Vṛnda was founded to change this.
about.storyPara4: We are not a Gurukulam. We are a trust that exists so Gurukulas can thrive — identifying what they need, sharing their story with a wider community, and working alongside them to build a sustainable future for Vedic education.
about.storyShlokaTranslation: May our minds be filled with auspicious resolve.
about.storyClosing: This resolve is our foundation: to serve the Gurukulas that preserve the Vedas, and to invite others to join us in this sacred responsibility.
about.visionText: A world where every Vedic Gurukula has the resources, recognition, and community it needs to thrive — and where the Guru–Shishya Paramparā continues to illuminate generations.
about.missionText: To identify the needs of Veda Gurukulas, create public awareness about their vital role in preserving Vedic Dharma, generate financial and community support, and foster their long-term growth and sustainability.
about.objectivesSubtitle: Our work spans six core areas of support for Vedic education and heritage preservation.
about.obj0Desc: Support Vedic education in Gurukulas, fostering saṁskāra, cultural values, and the cultivation of traditional arts and skills (kalā–kauśalya).
about.obj1Desc: Foster community engagement through the organisation and participation in awareness programs, workshops, and outreach initiatives.
about.obj2Desc: Support and participate in Vedic research initiatives and help build Vedic libraries for future generations.
about.obj3Desc: Assist Gurukulas in the fulfilment of their essential needs — infrastructure, teaching materials, student nutrition, and teacher welfare.
about.obj4Desc: Honour and recognise the sacrifice of Vedic scholars and Adhyāpakas who have dedicated their lives to preserving the Gurukula tradition.
about.obj5Desc: Support the development of Gośālās and the sacred cause of cow protection, shelter, and welfare.
about.operatePara1: The Vṛnda reaches out to Gurukulas across Karnataka — beginning with Bangalore — speaking with administrators, Adhyāpakas (teachers), and Vidyārthīs (students) to identify needs and assess what assistance can be provided.
about.operatePara2: In parallel, we are building a database of Adhyāpakas and Veda Vidyārthīs — shakha, level of study, contact details — for future reference and coordination. This systematic approach ensures that our support is targeted, sustained, and responsive to real needs.
about.teamSubtitle: The individuals who guide and govern the Vṛnda's activities.
about.anugrahaPara1: The name “Sri Shivasankalpa” was bestowed upon the Vṛnda as a sacred blessing by His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam of the Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri.
about.anugrahaPara2: Drawn from the Shiva Sankalpa Sukta of the Shukla Yajurveda, this name carries the prayer for a mind ever filled with auspicious resolve — and reminds us, in every endeavour, of the parampara in which we are humbly rooted.

about.anugrahaImageAlt: His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam of Sringeri Sharada Peetham

maharudra.imageAlt: Sri Adi Shankaracharya worshipping the Sphatika Linga — painting
maharudra.mapTitle: Hoysala Trust, Hosakerehalli, Bengaluru — venue for Maharudra Purascharana
maharudra.shlokaVedaTranslation: The particles of earth may be counted, the drops of rain may be counted — but even Brahma, the Creator, cannot measure the fruits of Vedādhyayana.
maharudra.introPara1: Recognising the immeasurable value of the Vedas, it is our sacred responsibility to contribute towards their preservation, nourishment, and propagation. With the boundless grace and divine blessings of His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahasannidhanam and His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam of Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri, and under the auspices of Sri Shivasankalpa Vṛnda, we are organising this Mahā Rudra Puraścaraṇa for Loka Kalyāṇa and the support of Veda Gurukulas.
maharudra.introPara2: We humbly invite all devotees and well-wishers to participate and contribute through tanu (service), mana (devotion), and dhana (resources).
maharudra.rudraTranslation: That which melts away suffering — that is Rudra.
maharudra.rudraDesc: Rudra is the compassionate Lord who melts away the devotee's sorrow and destroys all suffering.
maharudra.shivaPuranaTranslation: All sins are destroyed for one who chants the Rudra. Through the grace of Shiva's name, one crosses the ocean of worldly existence. The root causes of worldly bondage are undoubtedly annihilated.
maharudra.shivaPuranaPara1: As described in the Shiva Purana, the ultimate goal of human birth is liberation from the cycle of birth and death and attainment of Kaivalya (Supreme Liberation). In Kali Yuga, Bhagavan has bestowed two primary paths — Karma Mārga (Path of Action) and Jñāna Mārga (Path of Knowledge). Selfless actions performed with devotion lead one towards knowledge and liberation.
maharudra.shivaPuranaPara2: The Yajur Veda, particularly the Rudrādhyāya, prescribes sacred chanting and homa that remove accumulated karmas, bestow inner purification, and lead the seeker towards Amṛtatva — immortality.
maharudra.sevaSubtitle: Participate by offering seva. Each contribution supports the sacred event and the welfare of Veda Gurukulas.
maharudra.closingTranslation: May our minds be filled with auspicious resolve.
maharudra.closingPara: We earnestly request all devotees to participate actively and help make this sacred endeavour successful through your presence and support.
maharudra.cardSubtitle: For Loka Kalyāṇa and the support of Veda Gurukulas
maharudra.cardDescription: A three-day Mahā Rudra Puraścaraṇa organised under the auspices of Sri Shivasankalpa Vṛnda, with the divine blessings of His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahasannidhanam and His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam of Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri.
maharudra.day0Item0Desc: Deepa Aaradhana, Devatha Prarthana, Maha Ganapati Puja, Svasti Vachana, Deva Naandi, Panchagavya, Rakshoghna & Vastu Homa, Maha Mangalarathi
maharudra.day1Item0Desc: Kalasha Sthapane, Sahasra Modaka Maha Ganapati Homa, Mahanyasa Poorvaka Maha Rudra Japa (with Veda students), Rudrabhisheka, Maha Mangalarathi
maharudra.day2Item0Desc: Kalasha Aradhane, Kruchra Acharane, Maha Rudra Homa

gurukulaDetail.shrutiParampara_overview: Sri Shruti Parampara Gurukulam in JP Nagar is dedicated to preserving the oral tradition of the Vedas through the time-honoured Guru–Shishya Parampara. Twenty-three students undergo rigorous training in Veda adhyayana — Saṁhitā, Krama, Jaṭā and Ghana pāṭha — alongside Vedānga, Dharmaśāstra and supporting secular subjects.

gurukulaDetail.nammaSampradaya_overview: Namma Sampradaya Gurukulam at Varthur has been training students in Veda adhyayana for over a decade, with thirty residential students and one hundred and twenty alumni. Beyond Veda pāṭha, the Gurukulam emphasises Saṁskṛta, Purāṇa-Itihāsa and the practical art of public speaking — preparing Adhyāpakas who can carry the tradition forward.

gurukulaDetail.shankaraGurukulam_overview: Shankara Gurukulam, set amid the rural calm of Ungra village near Huliyurdurga, blends Veda adhyayana with the six darśanas, Āyurveda, agriculture and modern subjects. Twenty-two students learn Rigveda and Krishna Yajurveda alongside the philosophical śāstras, supported by an integrated curriculum spanning Saṁskṛta, science and computer literacy.

events.title: Events
events.subtitle: Sacred gatherings that strengthen community bonds and sustain the Vedic tradition.
events.introPara: Sri Shivasankalpa Trust organises events that serve both spiritual and social purposes — from elaborate Vedic rituals like the Maharudra Purascharana to community awareness programmes and Gurukula visits. Each event is an opportunity for devotees to participate through tanu (service), mana (devotion), and dhana (contribution).
events.moreEventsComing: More events will be announced as they are planned. Follow us for updates.

faqs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.subtitle: Common questions about the trust, our work, and how you can participate.
faqs.a0: Sri Shivasankalpa Trust is a charitable trust dedicated to supporting Vedic education in Gurukulas, fostering saṁskāra and cultural values, and sustaining the timeless Guru–Shishya Parampara. The name "Sri Shivasankalpa" was given as a blessing by the Jagadguru of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham.
faqs.a1: The word comes from the Shiva Sankalpa Sukta of the Shukla Yajurveda — "तन्मे मनः शिवसङ्कल्पमस्तु" (Tan me manaḥ śivasaṅkalpamastu) — a prayer that means "May my mind be filled with auspicious resolve." It reflects our aspiration that every action we take is guided by noble, dharmic intention.
faqs.a2: Donations support three primary causes: (1) Gurukula Abhivruddhi — direct support to Vedic Gurukulas for infrastructure, teaching materials, and student welfare; (2) Go-Samrakshanam — supporting Gośālās and cow welfare; (3) Event Seva — funding sacred events like the Maharudra Purascharana that benefit the broader community.
faqs.q3: How can I participate in trust activities?
faqs.a3: You can participate through tanu (physical service/volunteering), mana (devotion and spreading awareness), and dhana (financial contributions). Visit our Events page for upcoming programmes, or Contact us to learn about volunteer opportunities.
faqs.a4: We are in the process of obtaining 80G certification. Once approved, donations will be eligible for tax benefits under Section 80G of the Income Tax Act. We will update this page when the certification is in place.
faqs.q5: Which Gurukulas does the trust support?
faqs.a5: The Vṛnda is currently engaged with four Gurukulas: Sri Shruti Parampara Gurukulam (JP Nagar, Bangalore), Namma Sampradaya Gurukulam (Varthur, Bangalore), Shankara Gurukulam (Ungra, Huliyurdurga), and Sri Ramana Maharṣi Brahma Vidyāśrama (Madagondapalli, Hosur). We are actively expanding our network across Karnataka and beyond.
faqs.a6: We welcome volunteers for event coordination, Gurukula visits, documentation, and outreach. Please write to us at info@shivasankalpa.org with a brief note about how you would like to contribute.
faqs.q7: What is the trust's connection to Sringeri?
faqs.a7: Sri Shivasankalpa Vrunda was blessed and named by the Jagadguru of the Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri. The trust considers the blessings and guidance of the Sringeri Jagadgurus as paramount and operates in alignment with the Advaita Vedanta tradition of Adi Shankaracharya.
